pr_title: executor: close indexlookup executor in background
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: you06 <you1474600@gmail.com>

<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #29716

Problem Summary:

When closing the IndexLookUpExecutor, it'll wait until all on-flying requests are done, which will increase the latency of the next SQL execution, this PR makes the close jobs executed in the background.

issue_context.title: executor: SQL after IndexLookUpExecutor may be slow
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

- 1. Create a table with a non-unique index, generate about 10,000,000 rows(I use this [script](https://gist.github.com/you06/c4f5032b6492864e72afea2119207c85)).
- 2. Make an indexlookup query with limit, once it's done, do `select 1;`.
- 3. Repeat step2.

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

The `select 1;` query should be fast, at least less than 10ms.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```sql
MySQL [test]> select * from t force index(i) where c2 > 1 and c2 < 12000000 and c3 in (3) order by c2 desc limit 11; select 1;
+----------+----------+------+
| c1       | c2       | c3   |
+----------+----------+------+
|  2925230 | 11999949 |    3 |
|  4950694 | 11999947 |    3 |
| 11778881 | 11999851 |    3 |
|  2244706 | 11999851 |    3 |
| 10488089 | 11999821 |    3 |
|  5891917 | 11999812 |    3 |
| 11706844 | 11999801 |    3 |
| 10178503 | 11999619 |    3 |
| 13321140 | 11999576 |    3 |
|  5117855 | 11999563 |    3 |
|  9638867 | 11999561 |    3 |
+----------+----------+------+
11 rows in set (0.00 sec)

+---+
| 1 |
+---+
| 1 |
+---+
1 row in set (0.49 sec)
```

The `select 1;` costs about half a second.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

```

```
comments:
The root cause of this issue is when indexlookup reads enough data(there is a limit executor), it responds the result and success to the client. The client then executes the next SQL. However, when TiDB receives the next SQL(like `select 1;`), the connection thread may still be blocked by the `Close` function.

The `Close` function won't return until all requests are done.

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/a4bd02e35ce0f0236ae055984a65d38494a8e247/executor/distsql.go#L684-L685
do other executors have the same problem?

> do other executors have the same problem?

I took look at the [3 distsql executors](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/d3a4187f7e99a0c156912b6831686e89fc8b6a85/executor/distsql.go#L57-L61), and only find `IndexLookUpExecutor` has such a problem, not checked other executors yet.
Please check whether the issue should be labeled with 'affects-x.y' or 'fixes-x.y.z', and then remove 'needs-more-info' label.

Some situations could be simulated and the slow `close` may impact the query time much but we could not find useful information from the slow log, just like

The latency appears between two statements, so no statement will record it. Maybe a `wait_start_time` would be helpful in diagnosing.

review_comments: The atomic seems not enough here. When there is a response, if we check the atomic variable and make sure it's not closed yet, then we start updating the consuming memory and copr stats, just before the update is executing, the result is closed and there may be a nil dereference.
If the executor do not wait for task to exit, I'm afraid there will be some data race or chunk reuse problems....
What's the difference before & after this change?
Why this huge code block need to be under the lock? Is `fetchResp` called concurrently?
What's the difference check again here between checking in the next loop at line 578?
Close table reader before index worker, the index task may block on sending to the table task worker ... and then goroutine leak.
